title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Operating Procedures, and Top Support Issues
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook describes the standard approach for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation focused on SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical fixes for our top support issues. The goal is to ensure consistent, discoverable, and actionable developer-facing content that lowers time-to-value and reduces support load.

Audience

- SDK authors and maintainers
- Developer documentation writers
- Developer Support and Solutions Engineering
- Product and Platform engineers who own public APIs/SDKs

Scope

Covers: SDK guides (multi-language), quickstarts & templates, API example patterns, docs-site publishing and operating procedures, and a curated list of top support issues with canonical fixes and verification steps.

Standards and Naming Conventions

- File name format: short-descriptive with dashes, e.g., developer-sdk-python-quickstart-2026.json
- Document structure: short intro -> prerequisites -> step-by-step -> code examples -> troubleshooting -> ownership
- Code examples must include: copy-pasteable snippets, minimal config, and a brief explanation of security/permissions implications

SDK Guides: Structure and Required Sections

Every official SDK guide (per language) should include the following sections:

1) Introduction
- High-level purpose and recommended use cases.

2) Quickstart (copy-paste)
- Minimal example that authenticates and runs a simple request (e.g., text generation or embeddings).
- Should run with <= 10 lines of setup for the average developer.

3) Authentication and Credentials
- Supported auth methods (API key, OIDC, instance role), environment variable names, and example config.
- Security note: do not log keys; rotate every 90 days for permanent keys.

4) Common Patterns and Best Practices
- Batching, streaming, retry/backoff policies, and cost-control examples (token limits, stop tokens).

5) Advanced Usage
- Function/tool calling examples, structured outputs, long-context strategies, and memory/KV cache hints.

6) Error Handling and Retries
- Typical error codes, recommended retry windows, and idempotency guidance.

7) Testing and Local Development
- Unit test patterns (mocking network calls), local sandbox flags, and CI checks.

8) Reference (API surface)
- Parameter descriptions, defaults, and the contract between SDK and server.

9) Ownership and Release Notes
- SDK lead, package repo, release cadence, and link to changelog.

Minimal Python SDK Quickstart (canonical example)

- Prerequisites: Python 3.10+, virtualenv, REDWOOD_API_KEY set in environment

- Copy-paste example (should be present in every SDK guide):

```python
from redwood_sdk import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(text="Write a 2-sentence product summary for Redwood Inference.")
print(resp.text)
```

- Explanation: The example demonstrates authentication, a single request, and printing the resulting text. Replace REDWOOD_API_KEY with a short-lived key in production.

API Examples: Patterns and Languages

- Provide 1 canonical example per primary language (Python, JavaScript/Node, cURL) and one advanced example for server-side SDKs (Go/Java).
- Each example must show: authentication, a standard request (generation or embedding), streaming (where supported), and an error-handling snippet.

Canonical cURL example:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"Summarize Redwood Inference in one sentence."}'
```

Docs Site Operating Procedures

Purpose: ensure the docs site (documentation.next.redwood.ai) remains accurate, reviewed, and discoverable.

Content lifecycle

- Draft -> In Review -> Published -> Deprecated.
- Review SLO: content added as Draft must have at least one review within 3 business days and be published or commented within 10 business days.
- Owners must ensure examples run against the latest staging API (tag: docs-testing) before publishing.

Authoring checklist (must be completed in every PR)

1) Title and short description included
2) Quickstart example included and validated against staging
3) Code snippets have language metadata and are runnable when possible
4) Security/privilege notes added where applicable
5) Search metadata (summary, keywords/tags) present
6) Docs tests: linting + example validation (see CI docs-site job: docs/validate-examples)
7) Assign reviewer and set expected review SLO

Release process

- Minor content changes: merge to main, auto-deploy to staging, smoke-check by owner, deploy to prod within 24 hours of merge.
- Major changes (API surface or breaking examples): open PR, run example regression suite, schedule review with Platform and SDK owners, coordinate a staged rollout.

Docs Site Roles and Ownership

- Docs Owner: owns content accuracy and lifecycle for a given area (e.g., SDKs)
- DevEx Lead: coordinates cross-team reviews and drives doc quality metrics
- CI Owner: maintains the example verification jobs and SDK test matrices

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (current top issues observed by Support and Solutions Engineering)

Issue 1: Invalid or missing API key errors
- Symptom: 401 with message 'invalid_api_key' or 'missing_auth'
- Root cause: uninitialized environment variable or expired key
- Fix: confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY present and active; generate a short-lived key in Console -> API Keys -> Create; update env var and restart process
- Verification: curl with Authorization header succeeds (HTTP 200)

Issue 2: High per-request latency for small payloads
- Symptom: 95th percentile latency spikes for single-token requests
- Root cause: client-side batching disabled; TLS session not reused; poor region routing
- Fix: enable persistent connections in HTTP client, configure SDK persistent pool (see SDK config example), set region to nearest supported region in client constructor
- Verification: measure p95 in our telemetry and confirm drop by >30% after change

Issue 3: Streaming not working / partial responses
- Symptom: connection closes before stream completes or incomplete JSON chunks
- Root cause: intermediary proxies closing idle connections or incorrect chunk parsing in client
- Fix: upgrade to latest SDK with streaming fixes, increase proxy idle timeout, use chunked transfer parsing utilities provided in SDK
- Verification: end-to-end example in staging returns full stream and matches expected token count

Issue 4: Unexpected higher token usage/costs
- Symptom: invoices show higher tokens than expected
- Root cause: missing stop tokens, overly permissive max_tokens, or unintended input repetition from prompt templates
- Fix: add explicit stop tokens, cap max_tokens, and audit prompt templates for duplicated context insertion
- Verification: run cost-sensitive test harness and confirm token usage within expected bounds

Issue 5: Embeddings mismatch vs. baseline
- Symptom: semantic search recall regressions after a model swap
- Root cause: model variant differences or normalization changes
- Fix: pin embedding model in config, run offline evals (embedding drift test) and update vector indexing pipeline to match new normalization
- Verification: run evaluation harness and confirm recall >= baseline threshold

(Additional common issues: authentication for Private deployments, quantized model numeric drift, config drift between staging/prod; include per-area owners.)

Canonical Troubleshooting Template (use in Support KBs)

- Symptom (one sentence)
- Logs (copy of relevant log lines, scrubbed)
- Recent changes (deployments, config changes)
- Root cause hypothesis
- Steps taken / Fix applied
- Verification steps and telemetry to monitor

Documentation Release Checklist (pre-publish)

- Run docs linter and fix warnings
- Validate all copy-paste code snippets against staging
- Add labeling and keywords for discoverability
- Attach ownership team and slack contact in page metadata
- Ensure accessibility (alt text for images, keyboard focus examples for interactive content)

Metrics and Quality Signals

- Time-to-first-example success (goal: <= 10 min for 90% of users)
- Number of support tickets referencing docs (goal: reduce by 25% YoY)
- Docs-test pass rate in CI (goal: 100% for published pages)

Contact and Escalation

- Primary: devex@redwood.ai (triaged by DevEx team)
- Escalation: on-call SDK owner (see team roster)

Appendix: Useful Templates and Snippets

- PR description template for docs changes
- Quickstart template (README quickstart.md)
- Example verification script (scripts/validate_example.sh)

Example PR description template:

Title: [Docs] short description of change

Summary:
- What changed and why

Validation steps:
- Steps to validate locally and in staging

Owner: @team-or-person
Reviewers: @reviewer1 @reviewer2

Related pages:
- link to related docs or SDK repo

Last notes

Keeping developer docs high-quality requires partnership between SDK owners, platform engineers, and support. Use this playbook as the canonical source for how we author, review, publish, and maintain DevEx content. If you find missing quickstarts or repeated support patterns not covered above, open an issue in the devex backlog and tag the DevEx Lead.
